title: All in on aero: Cervélo Áspero-5 review

takeaways.text: Cervélo claims 37 W faster than the old bike at 30 mph; he notes the gap shrinks at realistic gravel speeds, and Cervélo supplied 20 mph calculations.
Livability compromises: the deep aero seatpost makes a saddle bag hard to fit and the down-tube storage is tight; the frameset costs US$5,500.
Sizing trends are modern: 170 mm cranks and a 40 cm bar on the 56, with a 48T chainring and 10–52 cassette on all builds.
The cockpit stays two-piece, so bar angle, width and stem length can be changed and it breaks down for travel.
Rated for 45 mm with about 6 mm per side, so a 50 mm tire could squeeze in but not for muddy days; chainrings up to 52T fit with a wide chainline.

disclosure: How the bike was supplied is not stated; Cervélo provided additional aero calculations at the reviewer's request.
summary: Ben Delaney's review of the 2025 Cervélo Áspero-5 aero gravel bike, including Cervélo's aero claims at realistic speeds.
